body: The current approach adds `gc * letterSpacing` to `width` and tries to trim trailing spacing via `lineEndFitAdvance = width - letterSpacing`. However, the line-breaker doesn’t consult `lineEndFitAdvances` when a line ends after a non-breakAfter segment (e.g., breaking before the next word/CJK unit), so lines can still include an extra trailing letter-spacing, causing earlier-than-CSS breaks and slightly inflated reported widths. Consider moving the trimming logic into the line-breaking step (e.g., when finishing a line, use `lineEndPaintAdvances/lineEndFitAdvances` of the last included segment) or otherwise ensure trailing spacing is removed for *all* line-end cases, including segment and grapheme breaks.

In the overflow-wrap path, `gc` is derived from `graphemeWidths.length`, but `getSegmentGraphemeWidths()` returns `null` when the segment is a single grapheme (e.g., combining-mark sequences like "e\u0301"), even though `text.length > 1`. That makes `gc=0`, so the segment’s cached `width` won’t be adjusted for `letterSpacing` in these cases. Consider falling back to `countGraphemes(text)` when `graphemeWidths` is null so single-grapheme multi-code-unit segments still receive spacing adjustments.
```suggestion
      const gc =
        letterSpacing !== 0
          ? graphemeWidths !== null
            ? graphemeWidths.length
            : countGraphemes(text)
          : 0
```

body:
Adjusting `graphemeWidths`/`graphemePrefixWidths` by adding `letterSpacing` to every grapheme advance bakes in a trailing spacing after the last grapheme. The grapheme-level breaking code in `line-break.ts` sums these per-grapheme widths directly and doesn’t have a trimming step analogous to `lineEndFitAdvance`, so wrapped lines that end mid-segment can be off by one `letterSpacing` and break too early. To match CSS, the line-breaking logic needs to subtract the trailing spacing at grapheme line-ends (or the precomputed grapheme widths need to encode spacing in a way that doesn’t require runtime trimming).
```suggestion
        graphemeWidths = graphemeWidths.map((w, i) => w + (i < gc - 1 ? letterSpacing : 0))
      }
      if (gc > 0 && graphemePrefixWidths !== null) {
        graphemePrefixWidths = graphemePrefixWidths.map((w, i) => w + i * letterSpacing)
```

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Keep preserved-space runs coalesced for pre-wrap hanging fit**

Preventing `preserved-space` coalescing here turns a space run into multiple segments, but the line breaker’s hanging-whitespace fit logic only excludes the current trailing whitespace segment from fit width. That means earlier spaces in the same run start counting toward fit and can trigger extra wraps (for example, `foo   bar` at a width just over `foo` can split into three lines). In `white-space: pre-wrap`, trailing preserved spaces are expected to hang as one run, so this change regresses browser-parity wrapping for multi-space runs.
